description: Estudiantes apa por la Inteligencia Artificial, la Visita Computacional y la arquitectura de software aplicada a la observación de la Tierra. Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar una plataforma web geoespacial impulsada por IA que proceso datos de radar de apertura sintética para identificar, medir y alertar automáticamente sobre deformaciones del terreno, deslizamientos y actividad volcánica en la región andina.
summary: AndesSAR is an interactive web-based early warning platform developed by EchoVision Labs that transforms complex NASA Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into clear, actionable insights for authorities and citizens in Arequipa, Peru. Addressing the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge, our system monitors three critical regional hazards where optical cameras fail due to clouds, volcanic ash, or subsurface processes: landslides in the Siguas-Majes Valley, volcanic inflation at Sabancaya Volcano, and cryosphere retreat at Coropuna Glacier. Using 13 months of continuous NASA OPERA Level-2 RTC-S1 radar backscatter data (Nov 2025 – Nov 2026), AndesSAR provides an interactive time-lapse player that tracks underground irrigation seepage and slope instability right next to the Pan-American Highway. By translating decibel variations into intuitive soil moisture alerts and dispatching one-click geotagged WhatsApp warnings to Civil Defense (COER), AndesSAR helps prevent infrastructure collapse and protects lives.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

AndesSAR bridges the gap between microwave radar physics and local disaster prevention in Arequipa, Peru. It monitors three multi-hazard scenarios:

- Siguas & Majes Valley (Landslides): Intensive flood irrigation on the Majes plateau filters underground through the permeable Millo Formation and emerges along the Siguas cliff, dissolving soil salts and triggering massive landslides next to the Pan-American Highway.

- Sabancaya Volcano (InSAR Deformation): Penetrates dense ash and gas plumes to detect pre-eruptive ground swelling.

- Coropuna Glacier (Cryosphere Retreat): Tracks accelerated ice melting and glacial lake expansion (Pallarcocha) to prevent outburst floods (GLOFs).

2. KEY FEATURES & CREATIVITY

- 13-Month Interactive SAR Time-Lapse (Nov 2025 – Nov 2026): Users can play or scrub month-by-month through a full year of real NASA OPERA-S1 radar backscatter evolution to see how seasonal summer rainfall (Jan–Mar) and agricultural irrigation saturate the cliff edge.

- Citizen-Friendly Translation: Translates technical SAR backscatter differentials (dB) and coherence into intuitive physical ground states (Red: Waterlogged Soil / Landslide Risk, Orange: Very Wet Soil, Yellow: Mild Moisture, Uncolored/Blue: Dry & Stable Ground) and equivalents in soccer fields.

- Dynamic Per-Anomaly Diagnostics & WhatsApp Dispatch: Clicking any of the 25 segmented polygons provides customized causal explanations ("Why it happens") and mitigation protocols ("What to do") per sector and month, with one-click geotagged alert dispatch via WhatsApp to COER Arequipa, AUTODEMA, IGP, and ANA.

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

We implemented a decoupled two-stage architecture:

- Stage 1: Batch Geospatial Processing Pipeline (Python on Google Cloud Colab): Using Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy, OpenCV, and Shapely, we ingested NASA OPERA_L2_RTC-S1 GeoTIFF rasters (Burst T047-100849-IW2, VV polarization), reprojected to EPSG:4326, computed multi-temporal logarithmic backscatter differentials, applied Gaussian smoothing and morphological closing, and vectorized the 25 high-risk anomaly polygons.

- Stage 2: Zero-Latency Web GIS Client (React 18, Vite, React-Leaflet): Deployed on Vercel with bilingual support (EN / ES), rendering multi-temporal raster heatmaps and interactive GeoJSON layers instantly even on low-bandwidth field connections.

4. INTENDED IMPACT & FACTORS CONSIDERED

Designed for regional emergency operators (COER Arequipa, AUTODEMA, IGP, ANA) and local farmers, AndesSAR enables early intervention—such as transitioning from flood irrigation to drip irrigation and installing cliff drainage—months before catastrophic slope collapse cuts off the Pan-American Highway.

5. ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) ASSISTANCE

In accordance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, EchoVision Labs acknowledges that AI/SI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot and Google Gemini) were utilized to assist in structuring React-Leaflet UI components, optimizing Python OpenCV raster-to-GeoJSON scripts, and refining bilingual (EN/ES) translations. All satellite data analysis, coordinates, and hazard models are grounded in real NASA OPERA-S1 datasets.
